formatRationale.reason: Published references carry documentId, referenceId and literal locators. One table per book in source-catalog.json stores document identity/hash/authority/currentness; the reference content ID protects the complete association. Scratch/unpublished metadata may use inline catalogs.
Distinguishes an accepted document from its corpus companion; their hashes must not be interchanged.

Inventories the original source-only fields of a flat document-bearing record. The inverse flattens these fields in original order; ordinary quotation, field, role, recipient and fact metadata remains inline.

A books/core/mfm/HTTP document path plus a locator resolves as a document, while its original sourceId field is restored by the layout. Its legacy sha256 remains attribute context because this form can hash fragment text rather than document bytes.

Preserves original literal locators. Opaque selectors and line numbers use TEXT_LOCATION; pages use PDF_PAGE with their original scalar or array values. Explicit xpath and JSON/HTML pointers retain their declared locator kinds.
An unregistered or ambiguous document remains explicit UNRESOLVED_SOURCE. Captured/canonical entity IDs alone are typed identity contexts, not unresolved document references.
Canonical rule/entity ownership is separate from document identity and source hashes.

Published binding tuples, value-free layouts and contexts are interned across snapshots. They preserve exact existing structures, captured identities, effectiveFrom and unpaired purpose-specific hashes. Catalog entries are validated before first use and frozen; replacing record metadata invalidates cached reads. Canonical currentness contains only sourceVersion, effectiveDate, observedAt and acceptedBaseHead. No legacy provenance object is duplicated.
